title: Sergiño Dest to leave USMNT camp with injury, out for Nations League quarterfinals
content:
U.S. men’s national team defender Sergiño Dest will depart camp on Friday and return to PSV due to a minor injury, U.S. Soccer announced Thursday.

Dest underwent a medical evaluation and is being “kept out of the upcoming matches as a precaution,” the release said.

Dest, 26, is a two-time World Cup starter for the U.S. and can play both right back and left back. He was set to be an experienced option for Mauricio Pochettino in the upcoming Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal games against Haiti.

The U.S. still has four fullbacks on the roster for the games: veterans Antonee Robinson and Alex Freeman, both of whom started at the 2026 World Cup; right back Bryan Reynolds, who returns to the senior team mix for the first time since the 2023 Gold Cup; and Nashville SC’s Reed Baker-Whiting, who is in line for a senior debut.

Dest’s departure could mean that Pochettino utilizes a more traditional four-man back line rather than the hybrid setup the U.S. played at the World Cup. There is flexibility to do so with more traditional wingers on the roster, including the Philadelphia Union’s Cavan Sullivan and Borussia Dortmund’s Mathis Albert, along with AC Milan star Christian Pulisic.

Robinson and Freeman will be the presumptive starters at the fullback spots, with center back Chris Richards likely anchoring the back line. Auston Trusty, Mark McKenzie and Neil Pierre are the other center backs on the roster.

Dest is the third player called in to camp that had to withdraw due to injury: George Campbell, replaced by McKenzie and Gio Reyna, replaced by Jack McGlynn were the others.

The U.S. will face Haiti on Nov. 14 at Nu Stadium in Miami at 4:30 p.m. ET, then host a return leg at TQL Stadium in Cincinnati on Nov. 17. The winner of the two-leg series will qualify for the 2027 Gold Cup and will also move on to the Nations League semifinals in March at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, Calif.
